documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six weeks out from the C. diff admission. Bowels completely normal. No fever. Appetite back, weight holding at 55. Energy better, out walking with her cane when it isn't icy.
Breathing: back to her usual. Hasn't needed albuterol since November.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P
C. difficile infection, resolved.
COPD, baseline; albuterol prn.
L femoral neck fracture s/p L THA, healed, doing well.
Osteoporosis: calcium, vitamin D, home exercises.
CBC/BMP today to make sure counts and kidneys have settled.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ruth, white count, blood count and kidney tests are all back to normal. Nice to see you looking like yourself again.

Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth each morning for 5 days

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Acute Visit - COPD
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Since Friday her cough has picked up, bringing up more thick sputum, and she gets winded making the bed. Using albuterol 3 or 4 times a day with some relief. No fever, no chest pain. Home COVID test negative x2.

Exam: vitals as charted, no fever. Mild end-expiratory wheeze both sides, no focal crackles. Speaking full sentences. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
COPD exacerbation, increased dyspnea, sputum volume and purulence.
- Prednisone 40 mg x5 days.
- Antibiotic given purulent sputum. Weighed the C. diff history; doxycycline is the lowest risk choice. 100 mg bid x5 days. Took it upright with water given her esophagus history.
- Albuterol as needed.
Call if no better in 3 days or worse sooner. If she gets diarrhea after this, call right away.

conditions.label: Severe Clostridioides difficile infection without toxic megacolon

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 10 days

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, 3/21/2022.

CC: diarrhea x3 days.

HPI: 76F with osteoporosis, COPD and C. difficile infection in November 2021. Three days of watery diarrhea, belly pain and low-grade fevers, 6 to 8 unformed stools a day. Finished doxycycline and prednisone for a COPD flare about two weeks ago. No blood in stool. Tolerating fluids.
PMH: osteoporosis with T12 fractures and L hip fracture s/p THA (2021); COPD; pill esophagitis; prior C. diff.
Meds: calcium, vitamin D3, multivitamin, acetaminophen prn, albuterol prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, minimal alcohol, retired teacher.

Vitals: T 38.2 C (100.8 F), HR 102, BP 135/85.
Exam: dry mucous membranes. Abdomen soft, mild diffuse tenderness, no rebound or guarding, not distended. 

Labs: WBC 15,000. Creatinine normal. Stool positive for C. difficile toxin and GDH antigen.

Course: 1 L IV fluid, heart rate improved to 88. Tolerating PO. Discussed admission; patient prefers home, husband present, able to drink. Reasonable.

Assessment: second episode of C. difficile infection, severe by WBC criterion.
Plan: fidaxomicin 200 mg twice daily x10 days (first dose given here). Hydrate. Return for worsening pain, distension, inability to keep fluids down or lightheadedness. PCP follow-up within a week.

documents.title: Fidaxomicin coverage
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy called: Part D plan requires prior auth for fidaxomicin. ED started it; PCP agreed to submit. PA submitted with diagnosis of second C. difficile episode, approved same afternoon. Pharmacy notified, husband picking up today. Pt has enough from the ED for tonight.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED record received, C. diff again. Pt on fidaxomicin, PA approved yesterday. Still 4 or 5 loose stools today, fewer than Monday. No fever this morning. Drinking broth and electrolyte drinks. Knows to return for belly swelling or lightheadedness. Video visit next Tuesday.

conditions.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit - Post-ED
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home, identity verified, consents.

ED 3/21 for recurrent C. diff two weeks after doxycycline/prednisone. On fidaxomicin since then, day 8 of 10. Diarrhea down to 1 or 2 soft stools a day, no fever since Thursday, eating toast and chicken soup and more. Drinking well.
Chest: cough back to baseline, no albuterol for a week.

A/P
1. C. difficile infection, second episode, responding to fidaxomicin. Finish the course. If it comes back again we'd talk about GI referral for further options.
2. COPD exacerbation, resolved.
3. She asked if she should ever take antibiotics again. Only when truly needed, and remind any doctor about her C. diff.
Office visit in 6 weeks.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
No diarrhea since finishing fidaxomicin at the end of March. Weight up to 56.5. Feels well. Gardening again, careful with bending, uses a kneeler. Hip excellent. No falls.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. L hip full painless range within precautions.

A/P
C. diff, resolved after second episode.
COPD baseline.
Osteoporosis on calcium/D.
AWV in September.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV.

Interval since last AWV (2020): L hip fracture with THA and rehab 9/2021; pneumonia 10/2021; C. diff twice (11/2021, 3/2022); COPD flare 3/2022. All recovered.

Function: independent in ADLs. Walks without a cane now. Back at the balance class. Husband drives at night. No falls in 12 months.
PHQ-2 0. Cognition: 3-word recall 3/3, clock normal.
Home: rugs gone, night lights, grab bars, railings both sides of the stairs.

Exam: vitals as charted. Kyphosis. Lungs diminished at bases, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema.

Prevention: high-dose flu and bivalent COVID today. Mammogram due in spring. Shingrix, Tdap (2016), pneumococcal complete. Colon screening finished.
Labs today.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Ruth, all your labs from Tuesday are normal: kidney, liver, calcium, blood count, cholesterol, and vitamin D at 33. No changes.

documents.title: Question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My dentist wants to know if I have ever taken a bone medicine like Fosamax, before he does an extraction. I took it for a few weeks in 2018. What do I tell him?

documents.title: RE: Question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Ruth, you can tell him you took alendronate for about six weeks in 2018 and stopped it that spring, nothing since. With such a short course long ago he should be comfortable going ahead. Happy to talk to him directly if he wants.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Good winter, no chest infections. Albuterol maybe once a month. Knees ache after the balance class, acetaminophen helps. Back stable. Weight back up to 57.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear, distant. Heart regular. Knees crepitant without effusion.

A/P
COPD stable. Knee OA. Osteoporosis on calcium/D. Mammogram ordered. AWV in the fall.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison 2021, 2019. Scattered fibroglandular densities. No suspicious mass, calcification or distortion. Stable.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Negative mammogram. Result released to portal and letter mailed.

AWV.

Quiet year. No hospital visits, no infections, no falls.
Function: independent, cooks, gardens, drives in daylight. Balance class twice weekly.
PHQ-2 0. Cognition intact by conversation and recall.

Exam: vitals as charted. Kyphosis stable. Lungs clear, distant. Heart regular. L hip well healed.

Well this year. No ED, no hospital, no falls. Independent. Walks 20 minutes most days, balance class. Celebrated 53 years married this summer.
